issue.title: Attachment discovery uses workspace owner/repo key instead of canonical project identity

task_type_fields.impact: Cold-cache agents cannot retrieve public or private bead attachments despite authorized shared storage. Cached bytes hide the bug. Normalize through canonical project identity for store/outbox lookup, preserve discovery error diagnostics, and add realistic managed-marker cold-cache read plus upload-discovery regression coverage. Respect the Rust shared-backend boundary; do not change attachment privacy policy.
task_type_fields.repro: From a managed bob-cli workspace on apollo, resolve_project_key(None) returns bobs-org/bob-cli; hidden_clone_path returns None and discover_shared_store(None) returns None. infer_project_name_from_cwd() returns gh_bobs-org__bob-cli, and supplying that canonical project_key discovers the existing private store. The land agent attachment path failed at 2026-10-09T19:15:22Z and after bead sync; athena SSH reading succeeded. The slash in the raw marker key is rejected by hidden_sidecar_clone_dir, then swallowed as no store. The same key shape reproduces for sase-org/sase.

issue.creation_reason: Investigating bob-cli-5z.land revealed that a valid private build-log attachment could not be fetched from a managed workspace. Independently reproduced the wrong project key and missing store for both public and private attachments.

payload.description: Both change attachment store discovery; this report concerns canonical project identity rather than honoring the disabled flag.
Both touch private attachment store discovery; canonical project identity and remote visibility verification require separate fixes.

evidence.note: Independent landing reproduction for proposed follow-up sase-1ou.5.1.3 note 3 at sase d1a576ab4e: sase bead attachment push sase-1ou.5.1.2 exits 1 with no attachment shared store. resolve_project_key(None) returns sase-org/sase; infer_project_name_from_cwd() returns gh_sase-org__sase. Source discovery returns the raw marker key before canonical inference. The fleet bundle is locally cached (SHA256 70cd3ea90a7f3f9109b2a2ace9db79400a3118048fe4422e95270e742ff13c28) and all 20 fixture tests pass, but successors on another host still cannot rely on cold-cache retrieval. This is corroboration of the existing discovery defect, not proof shared upload succeeded.
